requirements: Two independently powered MPR121 boards on independent I2C buses; physical left/right join. Read all 12 electrodes each, preserve individual health and stale data status. SRAM diagnostic only.
codegen_plan: Reuse unmodified licensed OpenCores byte/bit controller from supplied Tang Mega example.
I2cRegister transaction sequencer: 100 kHz, repeated START, every write ACK checked, final read NACK, bounded timeout resets/release bus.
MprScanner per bus: scan 5A..5D, reset/stop/configure, read back 5C..5E, burst 00..29, atomic commit, bounded retry. No unsupported multi-touch coordinate claim.
TouchpadDebug captures two immutable snapshots every 50 ms and streams 100-byte CRC-8 ASCII frames via existing 115200 UART.
Python parser validates CRC, ranges and frame length; App shows raw filtered/baseline/delta, status and tentative single-finger row/column centroid.
timing: 50MHz; initial100kHz compared with10kHz, final diagnostic uses10kHz. 100ms timeout;20ms idle+burst+verification. UART20Hz perboard.
safety: SCL/SDA only drive zero or high impedance. IRQ input only. No external Flash, debugger firmware, clock or calibration changes.
verification: Behavioral two-slave simulation with address scan/readback/ACK/NACK/timeout
Full UART decode checked against Python
App regression, corrupt/truncated frames, stale isolation
Gowin 50 MHz timing and pin report
Real SRAM and serial observation then controlled physical touches
observations: TP2 configuration readback correct but00..29 allzero with auto enabled and disabled.
